measurement is already started.

Reduce GC pressure in LinesCombiner by ~90%

The LinesCombiner uses the `Array#zip` method to merge both line
coverage arrays A and B together. This creates a new array, immediately
discarding A and B.

When we're combining a lot of files, this creates significant pressure
on the garbage collection because we're allocating a lot of intermediate
arrays.

For example, all GitLab unit tests emit about 328 MB of minified,
uncompressed `.resultset.json` files. If we use `SimpleCov.collate` to
merge them (using the default configuration), we invoke the GC over
1,700 times.

If we instead reuse the longest array A or B to merge coverage in-place
without creating a new array, we reduce the GC invocations to 55.

This results in a total reduction in GC time by around 90%. On my M3
Max, this reduces the garbage collection time with our unit test
coverage result sets from 2.78s to 0.32s. In total, we're observing a
total speed up of coverage merging in this example of about 25% (9.55 ->
7.05s).

Because both approaches of using `Array#zip` or updating the array
in-place are functionally identical, we can replace the former with the
latter without any other changes.

Fix race condition in resultset file writing that caused flaky tests

The .resultset.json file was written using File.open with "w+" mode,
which truncates the file before writing. If another process reads
between truncation and write completion, it gets empty or malformed
JSON, silently losing previously stored results. This caused
intermittent failures where merged reports were missing one test suite's
command name (e.g. showing "using Unit Tests" instead of "using RSpec,
Unit Tests"). Fix by writing to a temp file first, then atomically
renaming it into place.

Closes https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/815.

Fix flaky cucumber test caused by browser caching of coverage report HTML

Cuprite cached the Rack::Static response when visiting /. Scenarios that
checked the coverage report footer after merging results saw stale HTML
from a prior visit, causing config_command_name.feature to fail when run
in the full suite.

Fix misleading 100% branch/method coverage for unloaded tracked files

Files added via `track_files` that are never loaded/required reported 100% branch coverage because `SimulateCoverage` returns empty branch data, resulting in 0 covered / 0 missed = 100%.

Add a `loaded` flag to `SourceFile` (passed via `add_not_loaded_files`) and use a `not_applicable` state in `CoverageStatistics` to report 0% instead of misleading 100% for files that were never loaded. This avoids faking raw counts while still producing the correct percentage.

Remove docile dependency

Replace `Docile.dsl_eval` in `configure` with a lightweight inline
implementation that copies the caller's instance variables into the DSL
context for the duration of the block, then restores them. This
preserves the existing behavior (local variables via closure, instance
variables via copy-in/copy-out) while eliminating an external
dependency.

Make StringFilter match at path-segment boundaries

StringFilter previously used String#include? which caused filters like
"lib" to match unrelated paths such as "app/models/library.rb". Replace
with a regex that anchors the match after a "/" and checks the right
boundary based on the filter pattern:

* Trailing slash ("lib/"): requires a literal "/" after the match,
  matching only directory prefixes
* Contains a dot ("test.rb"): allows substring match within the last
  path segment, so "test.rb" still matches "faked_test.rb"
* Otherwise ("lib"): requires "/", ".", or end-of-string after the
  match, so "lib" matches "/lib/" but not "/library/"

Render HTML coverage reports client-side from static JSON data

Replace server-side ERB template rendering with a static single-page
JavaScript app. The HTML formatter now writes coverage_data.js
(a thin JS wrapper around the JSON coverage data) and copies
pre-compiled static assets. All rendering — file lists, source code
views, coverage bars, group tabs — happens in the browser.

This cleanly separates data (JSON) from presentation (JS/HTML/CSS):

* Delete ERB templates, Ruby view helpers, and coverage helpers
* Move all rendering logic into TypeScript (app.ts)
* Add static index.html as a pre-compiled asset via rake assets:compile
* Flatten formatter class hierarchy (5 classes → 3)
* Introduce JSONFormatter.build_hash for shared, side-effect-free
  serialization used by both formatters
* Eliminate double JSONFormatter execution when both formatters
  are configured

Emit root-relative paths in JSON coverage output

Per-file coverage keys, group file lists, and minimum_coverage_by_file
error keys now use `project_filename` (root-relative) instead of
`filename` (absolute). Consumers already have `meta.root` if they
need to reconstruct an absolute path.

The frontend's `shortenFilename` simplifies to stripping the leading
`/` — no more root parameter threaded through the render pipeline.

Warn when coverage.json is clobbered by a concurrent process

Record the time each JSONFormatter process loads as `PROCESS_START_TIME`
and, before writing `coverage.json`, compare the existing file's
`meta.timestamp` against it. If the file on disk was written *after*
this process started, another test run likely produced it — warn that
the overwrite will lose their data and point at `SimpleCov::ResultMerger`.

The check is zero-cost for the common case (no existing file, or an
older one from a prior sequential run) and has no state beyond the
existing `meta.timestamp` field.

Sequential re-runs do not warn: the prior file's timestamp predates
the new process's start. parallel_tests-style setups, where workers
share `PROCESS_START_TIME` but finish at different times, do warn
once the later writers reach format time.

Drop leading `/` from project_filename

The paths returned by `SourceFile#project_filename` are described as
"relative to the projects directory," but they began with a `/` because
stripping `SimpleCov.root` left the separator behind. Consumers of
`coverage.json` (and the `minimum_coverage_by_file` error line) can
reasonably interpret a `/`-prefixed path as absolute and resolve it
incorrectly.

Strip the leading `/` or `\` in `project_filename`, adjust the built-in
regex profiles (`hidden_filter`, `test_frameworks`, `rails`) and
`StringFilter#segment_pattern` to match segment boundaries without
requiring a leading slash, refresh the JSON fixtures and specs, and
remove the now-unnecessary `shortenFilename` helper from the HTML
frontend (which also sidesteps any Windows backslash concern).

Anchored user-supplied RegexFilters that relied on a leading `/`, like
`%r{^/lib/}` need to be rewritten as `%r{\Alib/}`. Noted in CHANGELOG.

Emit coverage.json timestamp with millisecond precision

The concurrent-overwrite warning compares the timestamp in an existing
`coverage.json` against `PROCESS_START_TIME`. `Time.now` has sub-second
precision, but `iso8601` (no arg) truncates to whole seconds on the way
out, so a sibling writer landing inside the same wall-clock second as
when we started could slip past the check.

Switch `meta.timestamp` to `iso8601(3)` so the round-trip keeps
millisecond fidelity, and update the JSON fixtures and the
`json_formatter_spec` assertion to match.

Remove CC_TEST_REPORTER_ID special case for JSON formatter

The default HTMLFormatter already writes coverage.json, so the env-var
trigger that pushed JSONFormatter onto the formatter list is redundant,
it just caused a duplicate write of the same file. With the special case
gone, `SimpleCov::Formatter.from_env` has no reason to exist, so the
default_formatter module and its spec are deleted and defaults.rb sets
HTMLFormatter directly.

Replace inline MD5 with Web Crypto SHA-1

The frontend only needs a stable, fixed-length, URL/HTML-safe ID per
filename, not a cryptographic digest. The 85-line inline MD5 routine
existed solely to reproduce Digest::MD5.hexdigest from the old Ruby-side
renderer.

Drop it in favour of crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-1') in its own module,
truncated to 8 hex characters. Web Crypto is async, so resolve every
file's id once at startup (precomputeFileIds) and let the rendering
pipeline keep its synchronous fileId() lookups.
Document why the frontend needs a hash function

Have JSON formatter own all derived metrics

Previously the frontend recomputed group/all-files totals by summing
per-file fields, and computed each per-file total_lines as
covered_lines + missed_lines. The JSON formatter already exposed full
stats for groups and the overall total — the duplication invited the
frontend and the formatter to drift on rounding or definitions.

Add total_lines to per-file output so it's no longer derived, and pass
the precomputed total/group StatGroups into renderFileList so the
totals row reads them directly. The formatter is now the single
source of truth for these metrics.

Capture process_start_time during SimpleCov.start

Was a JSONFormatter constant initialized at class-load time, which
could be much later than when coverage actually started (e.g., lazy
require) and lived on a formatter rather than on SimpleCov itself.

Move it to a SimpleCov.process_start_time accessor set in
SimpleCov.start, so it represents what it claims to. JSONFormatter
reads it from there; if start was never called, we skip the
concurrent-overwrite check rather than warn against a fake reference.

Restore capture_stderr helper used by JSON formatter specs

The helper was removed in 2729bdf when it had no callers. The
concurrent-overwrite warning specs added in f9b698a depend on it,
so the merged tip of main fails on every Ruby version with
NoMethodError: undefined method 'capture_stderr'.

Fix race when parallel workers copy static assets

When parallel test workers exit at roughly the same time, each one
calls HTMLFormatter#copy_static_assets against the shared coverage
directory. cp_r with remove_destination: true would have one process
unlink an asset (e.g. favicon_red.png) just before another process
also tried to unlink it, raising Errno::ENOENT.

Copy each file via a uniquely-named temp file in the destination
directory and then File.rename onto the final path. rename is atomic
on POSIX and overwrite-safe, so concurrent writers can no longer
race on the same path.
Suppress cucumber publish promo message

Add simplecov:disable / simplecov:enable directive comments

Mirror RuboCop's directive style for selectively skipping coverage of
specific lines, branches, or methods:

  # simplecov:disable line             (block; closes at matching :enable)
  # simplecov:disable method, branch
  # simplecov:disable                  (no args = all three categories)
  # simplecov:disable line some reason (any trailing text becomes a reason)
  # simplecov:enable
  raise "absurd" # simplecov:disable   (inline; just this line)

Block directives sit on their own line (possibly indented) and open a
region until the matching `# simplecov:enable` for the same category;
unclosed disables run to end of file. Inline directives trail real code
and only affect that one line.

Categories are independently tracked: `# simplecov:disable line` skips
those lines from line coverage but leaves any branches and methods on
those lines reported normally. The bare form is a shorthand for all
three.

Trailing text after the directive is treated as a free-form reason and
discarded — no `--` separator or other marker is required. As a
consequence, an unrecognised category name silently falls into the
reason bucket and the bare form takes effect (a deliberate over-disable
so typos surface in the report rather than silently disabling nothing).

Comment extraction goes through `Ripper.lex`, so directive markers that
appear inside string literals or heredocs are correctly ignored.

SourceFile collects the per-category disabled ranges from Directive,
then applies them in process_skipped_lines, process_skipped_branches,
and a new process_skipped_methods. Method gains a direct skipped! flag
and overlaps_with? helper paralleling Branch's API.

Deprecate `# :nocov:` (and the configurable `SimpleCov.nocov_token`) in
favor of the new directives. Each file that still uses `# :nocov:`
emits a one-time deprecation warning to stderr at load time pointing
at the recommended `# simplecov:disable` / `# simplecov:enable`
replacement. The toggle continues to work; it will be removed in a
future release.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1135.

Warn when results are dropped due to merge_timeout

Stale resultsets were silently discarded by ResultMerger, which makes
unbalanced parallel_tests runs hard to debug — the first group's
coverage simply vanishes from the merged report once the last group
crosses the 10-minute default. Emit a single stderr line naming the
excluded command names so users know what happened and can bump
merge_timeout if they expect the data to survive.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1167.

Floor (not round) the post-filter totals in HTML report

When a user filters the file table, the totals row re-renders via
updateTotalsCell, which used Float#toFixed(2) — rounding 763/777
to 98.20%. The initial render uses fmtPct, which floors. Switch the
filter-update path to fmtPct so a user who sets minimum_coverage to
the displayed number doesn't get a failing run on the next pass.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1115.

Enable subprocess tracking by default in the rails profile

ActiveSupport::TestCase.parallelize(workers:) forks worker processes
that each run a slice of the suite. Without the Process._fork hook,
the workers' coverage never reaches the merged resultset and the
parent records 0% for every file the workers touched, so subsequent
runs overwrite each other. The default at_fork block already restarts
SimpleCov in the child with a unique command_name; flipping it on for
the rails profile is enough to cover the parallelize fork model.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1067.

Use atomic rename for every HTML report write

In Nix and similar pure-build environments the gem's static assets
ship at mode 0444. The earlier static-asset fix wrote them through a
temp file + rename, but coverage.json and coverage_data.js still went
through plain File.write — which opens the existing path for writing
and so raised EACCES on the second run when those two files were
inherited from a prior run at the same read-only mode. Extract one
atomic_write helper and route all three writes through it. rename is
atomic and overwrite-safe, so the read-only and parallel-worker race
cases collapse into the same clean code path.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/741.

Treat single-group parallel_tests run as final

ParallelTests.last_process? compares TEST_ENV_NUMBER to
PARALLEL_TEST_GROUPS as strings. parallel_tests sets the first
worker's TEST_ENV_NUMBER to "", so "" == "1" is false and a
single-group run never identifies a last process. SimpleCov's
final_result_process? inherited that — ready_to_process_results?
returned false, the minimum_coverage check was skipped, and a low-
coverage build silently passed. Short-circuit when
PARALLEL_TEST_GROUPS.to_i <= 1 so the lone worker runs the final
work itself.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1066.

Drop long-deprecated methods

- SimpleCov::Filter#passes? (deprecated 2011) → use #matches?.
- SimpleCov.adapters (deprecated 2013) → use .profiles.
- SimpleCov.load_adapter (deprecated 2013) → use .load_profile.
- SimpleCov::Formatter::MultiFormatter::[] (deprecated 2015) → use .new.

Resolve track_files glob relative to SimpleCov.root

The track_files glob was expanded against Dir.pwd at result time, so
test runners that chdir (or CI scripts that invoke the suite from a
subdir) silently skipped the unloaded-file injection and produced a
different file set from a run with the same config. Use SimpleCov.root
as the glob base and as the path-expansion base so the result is
deterministic regardless of cwd.

Document the underlying Rails 7+ `eager_load = ENV["CI"].present?`
asymmetry in the troubleshooting section, since that is the proximate
cause for users who hit different totals between local and CI even
when track_files behaves correctly.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1106.

Allow SimpleCov.root('/') to widen coverage past the project root

UselessResultsRemover prunes Coverage.result by a root-prefix regex
before any SourceFile is built, and the :root_filter profile applies
the same boundary on the user-visible filter chain. Both regexes were
constructed as `\A<root>/`, which becomes `\A//` when root is `/` and
matches no real path — so a filesystem-root setup (e.g. a Docker
layout where /app and /test are siblings) saw every file dropped.
project_name had a parallel failure: File.basename(root.split("/")
.last) is nil for `/`, raising a TypeError before the formatter ever
ran. Construct the prefix by appending the separator only when it's
absent, simplify project_name to File.basename(root), and have the
:root_filter profile reuse UselessResultsRemover.root_regx so the
boundary lives in one place. The README example for "tracking files
outside the root" now points at widening SimpleCov.root rather than
clearing filters, since the early prune always wins regardless of
filter chain state.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/860.

Break the dogfood-shortfall message onto its own line

The RSpec progress formatter doesn't emit a trailing newline after
the last spec's dot, so the dogfood reporter's puts ran straight onto
the same line, producing output like "...Dogfood: line coverage…".
Prepend an empty line so the message stands on its own when the
threshold trips.

Restore multi-line coverage summary and align dogfood with production

The HTML formatter used to print the post-run summary in a multi-line
shape — one line per criterion ("Line coverage: …", "Branch coverage:
…", "Method coverage: …") — under simplecov-html prior to the April
2026 merge. The client-side-rendering rewrite that immediately
followed (71b2a366) deleted the multi-line `output_message` as a side
effect, replacing it with a single LOC-only line that dropped branch
and method stats from the summary even when those criteria were
enabled. Restore the historical shape and apply the same treatment to
JSONFormatter so both formatters describe whichever criteria are
turned on. Percentages still go through `SimpleCov.round_coverage`
(floor) so 22103/22104 keeps printing 99.99%, not 100%.

While here, route the dogfood reporter through the same
`ExitCodes::ExitCodeHandling` pipeline production uses: drop the
`silent: true` from the HTMLFormatter call so the new summary is
visible on every run, build a local CoverageLimits-shaped Struct from
`DOGFOOD_THRESHOLDS`, and emit the standard "SimpleCov failed with
exit N" warning when thresholds trip. Contributors now see dogfood
shortfalls in the exact format end users see — per-criterion
violation lines, lowest-coverage files, and the failure summary —
instead of a bespoke "Dogfood: …" line.

Extract Formatter::Base for shared HTML/JSON scaffolding

HTMLFormatter and JSONFormatter had carried duplicated copies of the
same boilerplate: identical `initialize(silent:, output_dir:)`, an
identical `output_path` accessor, and a structurally identical
`output_message` that differed only in a leading "JSON " on the
summary line. Fold those into a new SimpleCov::Formatter::Base that
the two file-writing formatters inherit from. A `message_prefix` hook
lets JSONFormatter add the "JSON " marker without duplicating the
template; HTMLFormatter inherits the empty default.

`SimpleFormatter` and `MultiFormatter` are deliberately not migrated:
the first returns a string and writes nothing; the second is a
meta-formatter that wraps others. `Base` exists for "formatter that
writes a coverage report to a directory and emits a summary line,"
which today is just HTMLFormatter and JSONFormatter.

One load-order subtlety worth noting: json_formatter/result_hash_formatter.rb
reopens `class JSONFormatter` (no superclass), so if it loads before
json_formatter.rb declares `JSONFormatter < Base` it would create the
class with Object as the parent and trigger a superclass mismatch.
Move the `require_relative "json_formatter/result_hash_formatter"`
to the bottom of json_formatter.rb, after the class is established,
and leave a comment so a future refactor doesn't hoist it back up.

Add per-file coverage lookup API and CLI

Expose Result#coverage_for(path) and Result#source_file_for(path) and
add a CLI for editor plugins, CI scripts, and MCP-style tools that
consume reports out-of-band.
Add `simplecov run` to launch a suite with auto-instrumentation

Add `simplecov open` to launch the HTML report

Tiny QoL wrapper around the platform's default opener (`open` /
`xdg-open` / `start`) so users don't have to type a file:// URL or
remember the path to coverage/index.html. Defaults to
coverage/index.html; --report PATH overrides.

Add `simplecov report` to print the totals row from the terminal

Same numbers as the HTML report's All Files row plus per-group totals,
for contexts where opening a browser isn't an option (CI logs, ssh
sessions, terminal-only workflows). Reads coverage.json directly so
it's a strict consumer of existing JSONFormatter output.

Refactor CLI dispatch into a COMMANDS hash

So adding more subcommands doesn't keep growing the cyclomatic complexity of SimpleCov::CLI.run. Subcommand modules now accept extra keyword arguments via `**` so the dispatcher can pass both stdout and stderr uniformly.

Add `simplecov uncovered` to list lowest-coverage files

Quick "where should I add tests next?" view: read coverage.json,
filter to files below --threshold (default 100%), and print up to
--top files (default 10) sorted worst-first. Editor- and lazy-CI-
friendly: no need to open the HTML report just to find the next file
to write tests for.

Add `simplecov merge` to stitch parallel worker resultsets from the shell

Wraps SimpleCov::ResultMerger.merge_results so a CI matrix that drops
one .resultset.json per worker can produce a merged resultset without
hand-rolling a Rake task. The simplecov library is lazy-required so
the read-only subcommands (coverage / report / uncovered) keep their
fast cold-start path.

Validate inputs up-front and surface per-file errors before the merge
runs, so "this file isn't valid JSON" / "no resultset entries" points
at the specific bad input instead of falling out of ResultMerger as a
generic "no mergeable results in input files". When two input files
share a command_name, log a warning — ResultMerger would otherwise
silently fold them together with last-write-wins on the timestamp,
which is easy to mistake for "no merge happened".

Add `simplecov diff` to print per-file coverage delta vs a baseline

Reads two coverage.json files (current + baseline) and lists the
files whose coverage moved on any enabled criterion, regressions
first. Line, branch, and method deltas all surface on the same row
when their absolute change exceeds a small noise threshold. Files
present on only one side are tagged "(new file)" or "(removed)".

`--fail-on-drop` exits non-zero when any file's line coverage
slipped, so this composes with CI as a "coverage of this PR didn't
drop" gate even when overall thresholds are still satisfied.
`--threshold N` filters out small deltas (useful when a baseline is
noisy); `--json` emits the rows as a JSON array for programmatic
consumption. Coverage keys with a leading `/` (from coverage.json
files written before the SourceFile#project_filename change) are
normalized so an older baseline still diffs cleanly against newer
reports.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/886.

Have the CLI honor .simplecov's coverage_dir

The CLI was hardcoding 'coverage/' as the base for every default
path (--input, --report, --output). For simplecov-on-simplecov the
report actually lives in tmp/dogfood/, so 'simplecov open' fell back
to a non-existent path. Walk up from cwd for a .simplecov, lazy-load
simplecov with SimpleCov.start neutered so a project whose dotfile
starts coverage doesn't trigger tracking + an at_exit hook just from
the CLI asking for a config value, and snapshot/restore coverage_dir
so we don't quietly mutate host-process state when the CLI is
exercised inline by the spec suite.

For simplecov's own repo, drop a top-level .simplecov gated on
ENV['SIMPLECOV_CLI'] (set by the CLI's loader) so the value reaches
the CLI but doesn't leak into descendant Ruby processes (the
eval_test fixture, the cucumber test_projects) that would otherwise
inherit it via simplecov's own walk-up auto-load.

Add `simplecov clean` to remove the coverage report directory

Quality-of-life wrapper around `rm -rf <coverage_dir>` that uses the
same .simplecov-aware resolution as the rest of the CLI, so it deletes
whatever the project's report dir actually is (e.g. tmp/dogfood/ when
run on simplecov itself, not the never-existed coverage/). --dry-run
prints the would-delete path so you can sanity-check before pulling
the trigger.

Add `simplecov serve` to serve the report over HTTP

Tiny static-file server backed by stdlib `socket` so no extra runtime
dep is needed just to view a local report on a CI box where file://
URLs don't work, a remote dev session over ssh, or a sandboxed
browser. --port defaults to a random open port; --host defaults to
loopback. Ctrl-C terminates the loop.

Defer to Minitest.after_run when SimpleCov.start runs after autorun

Rake::TestTask and Minitest::TestTask shell out as

  ruby -e 'require "minitest/autorun"; require "test/test_X.rb"'

so when the test file (or test_helper) calls SimpleCov.start, Minitest's
at_exit hook is already registered. at_exit is LIFO, so SimpleCov's hook
fires first and formats a 0% report before any tests run.

When install_at_exit_hook sees that Minitest is loaded with its autorun
class variable @@installed_at_exit armed, set external_at_exit and route
the report through Minitest.after_run instead. The opposite ordering
(SimpleCov first, Minitest second) is still handled by the existing
lib/minitest/simplecov_plugin.rb, which now no-ops when external_at_exit
is already set so the two paths can't both register an after_run hook.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1032.
Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1099.
Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1112.

Write the formatter status line to stderr instead of stdout

The "Coverage report generated for X to Y" line and its per-criterion
totals beneath it are diagnostic messages — not the program's output —
so they belong on stderr by Unix convention. On stdout they pollute
pipelines like `rspec -f json` whose downstream consumers don't know
how to filter out unstructured prose.

This also brings the formatters in line with the rest of SimpleCov:
the coverage-threshold warnings, "SimpleCov failed with exit N…",
the framework-not-recognized hint, and the merge-timeout exclusion
notice all already go through `warn` (i.e. stderr). The formatter
`puts` was the lone hold-out.

Users who want the message suppressed entirely can already pass
`silent: true` when constructing the formatter. Anyone parsing the
prose off stdout in CI can redirect with `2>&1`.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1060.

Colorize the diagnostic output by coverage threshold

Adds a small `SimpleCov::Color` module that colorizes ANSI-tagged
text on stderr (or stdout, for the CLI) when the relevant stream is
a TTY, with the usual `NO_COLOR` / `FORCE_COLOR` env-var overrides.
Thresholds mirror the HTML formatter so the mental model is the same
in both views: green for `>= 90%`, yellow for `>= 75%`, red below.

Coverage percentages in the formatter summary line, in the four
threshold-violation checks (minimum overall, minimum by file, by
group, maximum drop), and in the CLI subcommands that print
percentages are colored by band. Two terminal-only messages from
`SimpleCov` get whole-line colors: red for "SimpleCov failed with
exit N…", yellow for "Stopped processing SimpleCov…". CLI subcommands
accept `--no-color` as a per-invocation override.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1157.

Add remove_filter and clear_filters for managing default filters

`SimpleCov.start` loads three filters by default — root_filter,
bundler_filter, and hidden_filter — and there was no way to drop one
of them short of `require 'simplecov/no_defaults'` (which removes
everything, leaving the user to re-add what they actually wanted).
The hidden_filter (`/\A\..*/`) in particular surprises projects
that keep code in a top-level `.scripts/` or similar.

`remove_filter(arg)` removes any filter whose `filter_argument`
matches by value, so `remove_filter(/\A\..*/)` undoes the hidden
filter and the rest of the defaults stay in place. `clear_filters`
wipes the chain for users who want a blank slate. The README's new
"Default filters" section enumerates what gets loaded and how to
turn each piece off.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/803.

Filter test/features/spec/autotest directories by default

`SimpleCov.start` now loads the `test_frameworks` profile alongside
the existing default filters, so paths matching
`%r{\A(test|features|spec|autotest)/}` are filtered out of the
report. The test suite always executes 100% of its own files; counting
them inflates the headline percentage and hides what the user actually
cares about, which is application coverage.

This is a breaking change: projects that previously saw their test
files in the report will find them missing. To restore the old
behavior — e.g. to surface dead helpers in `spec/support/` — drop the
filter with `remove_filter %r{\A(test|features|spec|autotest)/}`.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/816.

Lower parallel_tests min_coverage scenario threshold

The previous default of `minimum_coverage 89` was sized against a
report that counted spec files (89.36% before). Now that the
`test_frameworks` profile ships in the default filter chain, the
test_project measures 81.48% on lib only and the 89 threshold trips
the scenario on every CI matrix. Pin the threshold to 81.48
precisely so any future regression in lib coverage will trip the
scenario — and the scenario keeps asserting what it cares about,
that parallel_rspec workers don't print coverage violations before
the merge.

Allow disabling line coverage

Line coverage no longer has primacy at the architecture level. It is
still enabled by default (and `:branch` / `:method` are still off by
default), but it's now possible to do a branch-only or method-only
run by calling `disable_coverage :line` after enabling whichever
criterion the project wants to measure. `SimpleCov.start` raises
`SimpleCov::ConfigurationError` when every criterion has been
disabled, since `Coverage.start` with no arguments would otherwise
silently produce no data.

`primary_coverage` adapts: it still defaults to `:line` when that
criterion is enabled, but falls back to the first enabled criterion
otherwise — so `minimum_coverage 90` resolves to whichever
percentage is actually being measured, not a stale `:line` reference.
The validation runs from `start_tracking`, after the user's
configuration block has applied, so a `.simplecov` that toggles
criteria in arbitrary order can pass through transient empty states
without false positives.

`SourceFile#coverage_statistics` still includes all three criteria
(letting per-file computation stay uniform); `FileList` is the layer
that filters down to the enabled set, so `coverage_statistics`
serves as the general-purpose mapping from each enabled criterion to
its `CoverageStatistics`. The JSON formatter and the console summary
line iterate over whichever criteria the run actually measured, so a
branch-only run produces no `Line coverage:` line, no `lines` key in
`coverage.json`, and no zero-padded line numbers in totals.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/845.

Tighten error classes raised by configuration and filter sites

`SimpleCov::ConfigurationError` is now the dedicated exception for
configuration-time mistakes — no formatter set, an unsupported or
disabled coverage criterion, a duplicate or missing profile, an
unrecognized filter argument type. Users can `rescue SimpleCov::
ConfigurationError` to catch the whole category at once instead of
matching on RuntimeError messages.

`SimpleCov.collate([])` now raises ArgumentError, since calling
collate with an empty array is API misuse rather than configuration.
The abstract `SimpleCov::Filter#matches?` raises NotImplementedError
to surface the "you forgot to override this in your subclass"
contract through the conventional channel.

Existing specs that match on message regexes keep passing; the
profile and filter specs were tightened to assert the new error
class as well, documenting the contract.

Capture the deleted-source subprocess's stderr

The deleted-source fixture starts simplecov and writes a small
report — and since the formatter status line now goes to stderr,
running the subprocess with backticks (which capture only stdout)
let "Coverage report generated for Test to .../spec/fixtures/coverage"
leak into the parent rspec run's stderr. Switch to `Open3.capture3`
and ignore both streams; the spec only cares about the exit status.

Adopt RSpec-4-compatible syntax

RSpec 4 removes top-level monkey patches by default and tightens
predicate matchers / verify_partial_doubles. Bring the suite forward
to that idiom now (still under RSpec 3) so the eventual jump becomes
a no-op:

- Every spec opens with `RSpec.describe` rather than bare `describe`,
  including the framework fixtures used by `return_codes_spec` and
  the RSpec specs in every `test_projects/` project.
- `external_at_exit?`, `previous_error?`, and `RegexFilter#matches?`
  return real booleans rather than truthy/falsy values, so
  `not_to be_*` predicate matchers accept their results.
- The faked `ParallelTests` stub declares `last_process?`; the
  `SimpleCov::ResultMerger` stub targets the real `:store_result`
  method instead of a non-existent `:store`.
- `.rspec` drops the deprecated `--color` and renames `--warning` to
  `--warnings`.

Show a concrete, relative report path in the status line

The "Coverage report generated for X to Y" line used to print the
bare absolute coverage directory. It now prints `coverage/index.html`
from the HTML formatter and `coverage/coverage.json` from the JSON

pointing at the entry-point file the user actually wants to open.

would be harder to read. Pathname#relative_path_from raising
(cross-drive on Windows, mixed inputs) also falls back to the

Base#entry_point_filename keep the bare directory display.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/197.

De-flake order-dependent html_formatter_spec failures

The "stays quiet on stderr when silent: true" example was caught by
`SimpleCov::SourceFile.nocov_warned`, a class-level Set that gates the
once-per-file `# :nocov:` deprecation warning. Under some seeds the
warning fired into the assertion; under others an earlier example had
already suppressed it. Migrate the generic `sample.rb` and
`json/sample.rb` fixtures (and the embedded source lines in the four
json output fixtures) to `# simplecov:disable` / `# simplecov:enable`,
since neither test set is exercising the `:nocov:` syntax itself. Drop
the now-unused `reject_nocov_deprecation` helper, and clear the Set in
`html_formatter_spec`'s before block so the remaining `:nocov:`
fixtures elsewhere in the suite can't reintroduce the same flake.

The three "output path in the header line" examples expected
"Coverage report generated for RSpec to …" but sometimes got
"Coverage report generated for Cucumber Features to …".
`SimpleCov::CommandGuesser.original_run_command` is class-level state
that `command_guesser_spec` mutated on every example and never
restored, and `SimpleCov.command_name` lazy-caches `CommandGuesser.guess`
into `@name` on first call — so the first formatter example to evaluate
`result.command_name` after `command_guesser_spec` ran locked in the
polluted guess. Wrap the spec in an `around` hook that saves and
restores the attribute.

Allow setting coverage_path independently of root

`SimpleCov.coverage_path` is no longer derived strictly from
`root` + `coverage_dir` — pass an absolute path to set the output
destination directly:

    SimpleCov.start do
      root '/source/checkout'
      coverage_path '/tmp/build/coverage'
    end

This unblocks out-of-tree build setups (CMake/CTest, Bazel, etc.)
where the report should land in the build directory rather than
under the source root. Without an explicit setter, the only way to
get the report out of `root` was relative-path trickery against the
default `coverage_dir`, and that only worked because `ResultMerger`
incidentally expanded the relative path.

An explicitly-set `coverage_path` is sticky: subsequent changes to
`root` or `coverage_dir` no longer wipe it. The directory is created
on the first call if it doesn't yet exist.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/716.

Add a bundled 'strict' profile

`SimpleCov.start "strict"` enables line, branch, and method coverage
and pins the minimum threshold for each at 100% — equivalent to
hand-writing:

    enable_coverage :branch
    enable_coverage :method
    minimum_coverage line: 100, branch: 100, method: 100

Convenient for projects that have already paid down coverage debt
and want a "no shortfalls allowed" config in a single line. The
profile drops the branch / method clauses on engines that don't
support those Coverage features (JRuby), so it still loads cleanly
there and just enforces line coverage at 100%.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1061.

Skip configured-but-unmeasured criteria in violation checks

`SimpleCov.minimum_coverage line: 100, branch: 100, method: 100`
used to crash at check time on JRuby because the runtime can't emit
branch / method data — `result.coverage_statistics.fetch(:branch)`
raised `KeyError` after the criterion was configured but the engine
silently dropped it.

`CoverageViolations` now looks up the per-criterion stats with `[]`
(via a shared `percent_for` helper) and silently skips when the
stats are absent. The config-time `raise_if_criterion_disabled`
check still catches the genuine "forgot `enable_coverage`" mistake
before we ever reach the runtime check, so the relaxation only
covers the JRuby-shape case.

With that, the bundled `strict` profile collapses to its natural
form:

    SimpleCov.profiles.define "strict" do
      enable_coverage :branch
      enable_coverage :method
      minimum_coverage line: 100, branch: 100, method: 100
    end

On CRuby all three criteria are enforced; on JRuby the branch /
method clauses silently no-op and only `:line` is checked.

Run CI on macOS and Windows

Adds a single MRI job per new OS via `matrix.include`: macOS and Windows on the latest stable Ruby (`ruby-version: ruby`), with `ruby-head` for the equivalent slots in unstable.yml. macOS runs the full `rake test`; Windows runs `rake spec` only, since the cucumber suite drives headless Chrome via cuprite/ferrum, the same reason JRuby and TruffleRuby already skip it. `rm Gemfile.lock` is pinned to `shell: bash` so the step is unambiguous under PowerShell. `timeout-minutes: 20` on both workflows ensures a stuck spec fails fast instead of burning runner-hours against GitHub's 6-hour default.

Several test-suite portability fixes accompany the new jobs. `.gitattributes` forces LF line endings so Windows checkouts don't introduce CRLF into fixture-comparison specs (`source_file_spec` line/encoding examples). `return_codes_spec` passes env vars via the `Open3.capture3` env-hash form — the POSIX `VAR=value cmd` prefix syntax doesn't work outside a Unix shell. The `filters_spec` helper now uses `File.absolute_path?` instead of `path.start_with?("/")`, which misclassified `D:/...` paths on Windows.

Two specs whose subject is Unix-only are skipped on Windows: the `ResultMerger` "blocks other processes" example (shells out via `IO.popen("ruby -e ... 2>/dev/null")`, a POSIX redirection cmd.exe can't parse — the parent would spin forever on `gets`), and the `UselessResultsRemover` example exercising `SimpleCov.root("/")`, since `/` isn't a meaningful filesystem root on Windows.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/940

Add expected_coverage and maximum_coverage thresholds

`SimpleCov.maximum_coverage` mirrors `minimum_coverage`: pass a Numeric
(applied to the primary criterion) or a per-criterion Hash, and the
suite exits non-zero with `SimpleCov::ExitCodes::MAXIMUM_COVERAGE` (4)
when the actual coverage is above the threshold. `coverage.json` gains
an `errors.maximum_coverage` block alongside the existing
`minimum_coverage` / `maximum_coverage_drop` entries.

The convenience `SimpleCov.expected_coverage` sets both
`minimum_coverage` and `maximum_coverage` to the same value, pinning
the suite to an exact figure. A regression fails per the minimum, and
an unexpected improvement also fails — your cue to ratchet the
threshold up rather than silently absorb the gain. The check reuses
the existing `floor(2)` tolerance on the actual percent, so a maximum
of 95.42 still passes when the actual is e.g. 95.4287; only differences
in the first two decimals count.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/187.

Allow per-path overrides in minimum_coverage_by_file

`minimum_coverage_by_file` now accepts String and Regexp keys alongside
the existing Symbol-keyed per-criterion defaults. String keys match the
project-relative path exactly, except those ending in `/`, which match
as a directory prefix; Regexp keys are tested against the project path.
Per-path values may be a Numeric (primary criterion) or a per-criterion
Hash, e.g. `minimum_coverage_by_file line: 70, 'app/critical.rb' => 100`.

For each file, the effective threshold is the Symbol-keyed defaults
merged with every matching override — later overrides win per criterion,
and any override wins over the default for the same criterion. A file
that matches no override keeps the global defaults, so adding an
override only ever raises the bar for the files it touches. The new
overrides surface in `coverage.json` under the existing
`errors.minimum_coverage_by_file` block.

The public getter `SimpleCov.minimum_coverage_by_file` still returns
just the Symbol-keyed defaults, preserving the existing return shape;
a new `SimpleCov.minimum_coverage_by_file_overrides` reader exposes the
per-path map. The setter, `CoverageViolations.minimum_by_file`, the
`MinimumCoverageByFileCheck` constructor, the `CoverageLimits` struct,
and the JSON formatter were updated to carry overrides through.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/575.

Stop rake parents from clobbering subprocess reports

Three layers of defense end a long-standing failure mode where a parent
process — typically a Rakefile or a Rails app whose `Bundler.require`
pulls in simplecov — auto-loaded `.simplecov`, started `Coverage`, then
shelled out to the test runner. The subprocess wrote a correct report
on its way out; the parent's `at_exit` hook then formatted its own
empty result on top, wiping the data.

First, `.simplecov` is now a pure configuration file. The autoloader
wraps the load in `SimpleCov.with_dot_simplecov_autoload`, and any
`SimpleCov.start` call inside the file is intercepted: its profile and
block are applied via `initial_setup` (configuration only), and a
one-time deprecation warning points users at moving the call into
`spec_helper.rb` / `test_helper.rb`. No `Coverage.start`, no at_exit
hook, no empty parent report.

Second, `ResultMerger.store_result` now merges incoming entries with
same-`command_name` entries whose timestamp is `>=` our
`process_start_time`. Those entries can only have been written by a
sibling test runner that finished while we were running, so combining
coverage data preserves the subprocess's contribution even when an
empty parent result is stored over it.

Third, `SimpleCov.at_exit_behavior` defers entirely when our merged
result has zero files and `coverage/.last_run.json` is fresher than
this process. With the first two layers in place this rarely fires,
but it catches degenerate cases (merging disabled, custom formatters
that bypass the resultset) where the first two can't help.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/581.

Align track_files line classification with loaded files

Files added via `SimulateCoverage` (i.e., `track_files` matches that
were never required) used to run through `LinesClassifier`, which marks
every non-blank, non-comment line as relevant. Ruby's `Coverage` module
is smarter: it knows multi-line statements like a `@x = a.foo.bar.baz`
method chain are one logical line, that bare `end` keywords aren't
relevant, etc. The two paths disagreed, so the same file produced
different relevant-line counts depending on whether it was loaded.

`SimulateCoverage` now asks `Coverage.line_stub` for the classification
the runtime would have produced if the file were required, then overlays
`# :nocov:` toggles and `# simplecov:disable line` directive ranges via
`LinesClassifier`. `Coverage.line_stub` doesn't know about SimpleCov's
exclusion comments, so the overlay demotes those lines to nil; together
the two stages produce a stub indistinguishable from the loaded-file
result. When `Coverage.line_stub` raises (missing file, parse error)
the call falls back to `LinesClassifier` alone.

The cucumber fixtures had their expected percentages updated to reflect
the (now consistent) classification: untested files no longer count
`end` keywords toward "relevant lines", so totals shift accordingly.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/654.

Warn when collate drops missing source files

`SimpleCov::Result#build_source_file` silently skips entries whose
absolute paths aren't on the local filesystem, so a `SimpleCov.collate`
invocation run from a machine — or working directory — different from
where the individual resultsets were generated produces an empty
`0 / 0 (100.00%)` report that looks like success but isn't. Result
now collects those dropped paths and emits a single yellow warning
once the file list is built.

The wording adapts to the failure mode. When every entry in the input
was dropped (the cross-machine collate case), the warning explicitly
says "all N source file(s)" and reminds the user that `SimpleCov.collate`
needs the sources at the same absolute paths the resultsets were
generated against. When only some entries were dropped — the more
mundane "the file moved or was deleted since the resultset was
written" case — it stays quieter. In both cases up to five paths are
listed inline with a `(+N more)` suffix to cap the noise.

Adds `spec/fixtures/three.rb` (a three-line file with a leading
comment plus two `puts` calls) so the existing pre-0.18 resultset
test in `spec/result_merger_spec.rb`, which feeds that path through
`SimpleCov::Result`, no longer trips the new warning.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/980.

Stringify Result coverage keys without JSON round-trip

`SimpleCov::Result#build_source_file` deep-cloned each file's coverage
hash with `JSON.parse(JSON.dump(coverage))` to normalize symbol keys
(from the live `Coverage.result`) to strings (the shape `SourceFile`
expects). For resultsets loaded from disk that are already string-keyed,
notably the `SimpleCov.collate` hot path, the round-trip was pure
overhead, and even for the live result it allocated a full deep copy
when only the three outer keys need touching.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/916.

Redesign configuration DSL around cover/skip/group

Replace the 60-method configuration grab bag with a smaller, consistent
vocabulary: `cover` (the long-requested positive scope counterpart to
`add_filter`, with string-glob semantics that match `track_files`),
`skip` (renamed `add_filter`), `group` (renamed `add_group`),
`no_default_skips`, `merging`, `merge_subprocesses`, `print_errors`, and
a variadic `enable_coverage` that accepts `:eval`. Every legacy method
continues to work but emits a deprecation warning naming the exact
replacement and the user's actual arguments.

Tighten DSL-redesign deprecation warnings and migrate README examples

`SimpleCov.cover_globs` now walks into `ArrayFilter` wrappers, so a glob
nested inside `cover(["lib/**/*.rb", /helper\.rb\z/])` again drives the
unloaded-file discovery pass instead of being silently dropped.

The deprecation warnings emitted by `track_files`, `add_filter`, and
`add_group` no longer suggest replacements that would themselves raise:
`track_files(nil)` points at `SimpleCov.cover_filters.clear` (not the
invalid `cover nil`), and the block forms of `add_filter` / `add_group`
print `SimpleCov.skip { ... }` / `SimpleCov.group "Other" { ... }` rather
than interpolating `nil` from the missing positional argument.

README examples throughout the document — default filters, custom
filters, groups, root override, multi-runner collate, subprocess docs,
error-message suppression, the bundled `rails` illustration, custom
profiles, the FAQ section — are migrated to the new `skip` / `group` /
`cover` / `merging` / `merge_subprocesses` / `print_errors` /
`enable_coverage :eval` spellings, so copy-pasted snippets no longer
produce warning-spewing configs.
bundle update

Add ignore_branches for synthetic else branches

Ruby's Coverage library reports an `:else` branch for several syntactic
constructs even when the source has no literal `else` keyword:
exhaustive `case/in` pattern matches, `case/when` without an `else`
arm, `||=` / `&&=`, and `if` / `unless` without an `else`. Those
synthetic branches show up as missed and depress branch-coverage
percentages despite there being no source code to test against.

Only `:implicit_else` is supported today, but the variadic shape leaves
room for future synthetic branch types without an API change. Unknown
tokens raise `SimpleCov::ConfigurationError` immediately to catch typos.

The detection signal is structural rather than textual. An earlier draft
scanned the source at the branch's reported `start_col` for the word
`else`, but `Coverage` reports the position of the *body* of an explicit
`else` arm (e.g. `:nope` on the line below the keyword), not the keyword
itself, so the heuristic mis-classified explicit elses as synthetic. The
shipped check compares `start_line` against the parent condition's
`start_line`: a synthetic else inherits its parent's range and matches,
while an explicit `else` arm carries its own line number. This matches
every existing branch fixture in the spec suite (case,
case_without_else, nested_branches, branches, inline, elsif,
branch_tester) without source-text scanning.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1033.

Document explicit receiver in .simplecov file

In the next version of simplecov, all method calls in .simplecov must
have an explicit `SimpleCov` receiver.
Use load_profile shorthand in the .simplecov example

Switch parallel_tests final-result process from last to first

`SimpleCov.final_result_process?` now picks `first_process?` rather than
`last_process?` for the worker that waits for siblings and runs the
final result-merging pass. This aligns with the convention
parallel_tests's own README recommends: user code that has its own
`wait_for_other_processes_to_finish` in `RSpec.after(:suite)`
overwhelmingly uses `first_process?`, so picking the same side
eliminates the cross-process deadlock.

Side benefit: the previous `PARALLEL_TEST_GROUPS.to_i <= 1` short-circuit
(https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1066) drops out.
`first_process?` tests for the empty-string `TEST_ENV_NUMBER` that
parallel_tests sets on the only/first worker, so single-group runs are
correctly identified as final without the count fallback.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/922.

Fix HTML report group-id collision for similar group names

`toHtmlId` in the HTML frontend stripped every non-letter prefix and
then every remaining non-alphanumeric char from a group title, so two
groups whose names differ only in a leading non-letter (e.g. `">100LOC"`
and `"<10LOC"`) both sanitized to the same id (`"LOC"`). The container
`<div id>` collided, the tab `<a>`'s `className` collided, and the
second group's content silently replaced the first in the rendered
report — the underlying `Result` data was correct, only the JS-side
DOM rendering was broken.

Encode each non-id char as `_<hex codepoint>_` instead, prefixed with
`g-` so the id always starts with a letter. The encoding preserves
uniqueness across any input shape (including emoji and non-ASCII
group names) while keeping the result a valid CSS class name for the
`.group_tabs a.<id>` selector. The corresponding Ruby-side mirror in
`features/step_definitions/html_steps.rb` is updated to match, and
a regression scenario in `rspec_groups_and_filters_complex.feature`
exercises the previously-colliding shape.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1038.
