changelog_uri metadata now points at docs/Changelog.md. Every
cross-document link was rewritten and verified to resolve with a
case-exact check, anchors included.

Add a colorblind-friendly mode and non-color coverage symbols

Red and green are the report's core signal, covered versus missed, and
they are the pairing most colorblind viewers cannot tell apart. This
adds two independent ways to read coverage without relying on that
distinction.

A Colorblind toggle sits to the left of the Dark toggle in the toolbar.
It swaps the covered and missed colors, and the coverage bands, for
blue versus orange, the standard colorblind-safe pairing, in both the
light and dark themes. Skipped stays yellow and the branch and method
misses keep their orange and purple, since those already read as
distinct hues. The choice persists in localStorage and is applied
before first paint so there is no flash, mirroring the Dark toggle.

The source view now also carries a non-color marker in a left gutter on
every line: plus for covered, minus for missed, tilde for skipped, plus
or minus for a missed branch, and an f for an uncalled method. The same
glyphs appear on the legend swatches, so the mapping is legible in
greyscale and to assistive tech regardless of the palette. This is on
in every mode, not just colorblind, and was the maintainers' suggestion
on the issue.

Accessibility touch-ups alongside: both toggles report state with
aria-pressed, the dark toggle gains an aria-label, and a visible
focus-visible ring is drawn on keyboard-focused controls.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/534.

Address review: dark toggle role and print palette

Two fixes from the PR review.

The dark toggle carried aria-pressed while its accessible name flipped
with state (Switch to dark mode / Switch to light mode). aria-pressed
needs a stable name to be meaningful, so drop it: the button is an
action button whose label names the action, and the label stays in
sync with the visible text (which also satisfies WCAG 2.5.3 Label in
Name, where a fixed name would not). The colorblind toggle, whose
label never changes, keeps aria-pressed.

The dark colorblind overrides outrank the print reset that forces a
light palette, so a report printed in dark plus colorblind mode kept
dark covered/missed backgrounds while the rest of the page went light.
Scope the dark colorblind values to screen so they never reach paper,
and re-assert the light colorblind values inside the print reset so a
colorblind report prints blue and orange rather than reverting to the
green and red its reader configured away.

Repeat the mode toggles in the source file view

The colorblind and dark toggles lived only in the report's toolbar,
which the source dialog covers while it is open, so a reader could not
switch modes without closing the file first. Add both toggles to the
dialog header as well.

The two copies are wired by a data-toggle attribute rather than an id,
and each kind shares one click handler with all its buttons synced, so
toggling from either place updates the palette and both buttons at
once. The dialog copies are hidden in print like the toolbar.
Bump version to 1.1.0

Drive the final-result gate spec through real state

The stays-silent-when-not-the-final-result-process spec stubbed
SimpleCov.final_result_process? with a partial double, and on JRuby
the original method was still intermittently reached, apparently
through an already-compiled call site, so the missing-source-files
warning printed and the suite failed (seen on the v1.1.0 CI run,
unreproducible locally with the same seed and example set). A forked
subprocess is never the final-result process, so the spec now marks
the real forked-subprocess flag instead of stubbing, which exercises
the same gate through state no call-site optimization can bypass.

Move the issue template to .github where GitHub finds it

Relocating ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md into docs/ broke it: GitHub only honors
the docs folder for pull request templates, while issue templates are
recognized in the repository root, the hidden .github directory, and
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE. The move to docs/ was based on conflating
those two rule sets. The template now lives in .github/ alongside the
workflows and Dependabot config, keeping the root clean, with the
conventional uppercase name since the docs/ naming scheme doesn't
apply there. The 1.1.0 changelog entry describing the restructure is
corrected to match.

Stop packaging the schemas directory

Nothing reads schemas/ from the installed gem. The JSON formatter points
consumers at the canonical schema URL on GitHub and the schema specs read
from the repository, so the two schema files were dead weight in the
package. Dropping them removes 32 KB unpacked from every install.

Add end-to-end coverage for rspec-conductor parallel runs

rspec-conductor marks each forked worker with the parallel_tests
environment convention, TEST_ENV_NUMBER per worker plus
PARALLEL_TEST_GROUPS for the worker count (since rspec-conductor 1.0.7).
SimpleCov's generic parallel adapter already recognizes that convention,
so coverage from a conductor run merges into one report with unique
suite names per worker and no configuration.

Lock that support in with a dedicated test project and cucumber feature
covering the default numbering (first worker ""), the --first-is-1
numbering, branch coverage, and threshold checks deferred to the merged
report. Name rspec-conductor in the adapter docs so users can find it.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1156.

Share the parallel fixture between the parallel_tests and rspec-conductor features

The rspec_conductor test project was a byte-for-byte copy of the
parallel_tests one, differing only in which parallel runner its Gemfile
pulls in, and its feature repeated the expected coverage tables inline
three times. Any change to the fixture sources would have required
updating five copies of the tables and ten duplicated files.

Slim test_projects/rspec_conductor down to its Gemfile and Gemfile.lock.
A new setup step overlays those onto another project's sources, so the
conductor feature now runs against the parallel_tests fixture itself.
Rename the shared assertion steps to "the parallel fixture project"
(and their file to parallel_fixture_steps.rb) since they no longer
belong to a single feature, and reuse them in place of the inline
tables.

Keep exit tasks alive when a runner closes worker stdio before at_exit

rspec-conductor closes each worker's output pipes as soon as the worker
has sent its run summary to the server, before the worker's at_exit
hooks run. SimpleCov's exit tasks then died half way: the HTML and JSON
report files were already written, but emitting the status line probes
Color.enabled?, whose IO#tty? call raises IOError on a closed stream.
That exception aborted the rest of the at_exit work, so the minimum and
maximum coverage checks silently never ran under rspec-conductor, and
.last_run.json and the .report_stamp deferral marker were never written.

Treat a closed stream as not a tty in Color.enabled?, and drop the
status line in Formatter::Base#emit_status and the violation report in
ExitCodes.print_error when stderr is closed, instead of letting the
IOError cancel the threshold checks that follow.

The conductor feature's threshold scenario previously asserted that no
violation appears in the output, which the closed pipes made vacuous:
the text could never appear, and the swallowed worker exit status meant
the run always succeeded. It now asserts that .last_run.json carries
the merged 81.48. SimpleCov writes that file only when the threshold
check passes, and every single worker's partial slice is below the
threshold, so the file proves the check ran against the merged result.

Require coverage where Coverage.line_stub is called

SimulateCoverage and ResultAdapter both call Coverage.line_stub but
neither requires the coverage library, so they only work when another
code path has loaded it first. In a normal run start_tracking does
that, but a collate-only process never starts tracking. Today the
constant resolves by luck: the criterion-support check that
UnloadedFileInjector triggers happens to require coverage before the
line_stub call. Any reordering of that path turns into a NameError out
of SimpleCov.collate, so each file now requires what it uses.

Use anonymous block forwarding in the merge reference helper

The named block parameter added nothing: both methods only pass the
block straight through. Anonymous block forwarding works on every
supported Ruby (it arrived in Ruby 3.1), verified with a syntax check
and a smoke run on Ruby 3.2.11, and RuboCop's Naming/BlockForwarding
asks for this form once TargetRubyVersion reaches 3.4.

Add a bun test suite enforcing 100% coverage of the HTML frontend

The viewer's TypeScript modules are now tested with bun's built-in
runner against happy-dom, and bunfig.toml enforces 100% line and
function coverage on every run, the frontend counterpart of the
dogfood threshold the RSpec suite applies to lib/. The default rake
task and the typecheck workflow run the suite, and tsc now
type-checks the tests alongside the source.

Replace the cucumber feature suite with RSpec sandbox specs

Port every feature to spec/sandbox, driving the test_projects fixtures
in subprocesses through the SandboxProject harness. Browser assertions
become data assertions on the report payload embedded in index.html,
with rendering covered by the bun frontend suite.

Remove the browser-driving Aruba, Capybara, Cuprite, and Cucumber task
stack, the headless Chrome CI dependency, and the split CI test steps.
Keep Cucumber and Minitest as lightweight development dependencies
because copied fixture projects exercise their integrations from the
shared bundle cache.

Give each fixture subprocess a fresh Bundler activation with an explicit
copied or host Gemfile while retaining the host bundle path and excluded
groups. Cover both Gemfile paths so clean CI cannot leak the host
definition or lose its cached gems. The sandbox specs keep the old
platform envelope by skipping on non-MRI engines and Windows.

Fan the RSpec suite out across parallel workers

`rake spec` now runs the suite through parallel_rspec. The sandbox
specs spend nearly all their time waiting on fixture subprocesses, so
the suite parallelizes almost linearly (68 seconds serial, 17 in
parallel here), with a serial fallback where parallel_tests isn't
installed. Each worker scrubs the parallel_tests environment at boot
so command guessing, final-result detection, and spawned subprocesses
behave exactly as in a serial run, and per-worker tmp paths keep
coverage caches and warning captures apart. The dogfood coverage check
is now parallel-aware. Every worker stores its coverage slice as a
resultset-shaped partial, and the first worker waits for its siblings,
merges the slices through ResultMerger, and enforces the thresholds on
the union. Specs that asserted the literal tmp/coverage path now read
the configured directory.

Build a Rails-style screenshot coverage fixture

Add a self-contained RSpec project that generates fourteen realistic
Rails-convention files across every group in the rails profile. The
fixture keeps each source file near one screen while spanning the useful
line-coverage bands.

Enable line, branch, and method coverage with deliberately different
per-file values, and verify the file count, group tabs, criteria,
percentage spread, and source sizes before pointing the user at the
generated report.

Polish the source file view

Keep the colorblind and theme controls at the same viewport coordinates
as the index toolbar, reserve the close-button slot on the index, and
use the report background behind both copies. Reserve the scrollbar
gutter as well, so locking the page behind the dialog cannot reclaim
its width and slide those controls sideways.

Lay each source legend key on the same row as its line, branch, or
method summary, align the rows beneath the close button, and repeat the
generated-at footer at the bottom of the source dialog. Return the
header to document flow on paper, where the toggles and close button
are hidden and the legend reads better at full width. Add DOM and CSS
contract tests for the shared controls, legend grid, and footer markup.

Remember the file-list sort order

Persist the selected column and direction in guarded localStorage so
reloading a report restores the user’s sort across the All Files and
group tables. The guard around storage now lives in one module that the
display-mode toggles share.

Store semantic column keys rather than numeric positions, which lets
reports with different enabled criteria reject stale preferences and
fall back to the primary coverage sort. Break equal values by filename
so the restored order exactly matches the clicked order. Give the
covered and total columns a sort value of their own, because their
displayed digits are comma grouped and would otherwise rank 1,250 below
999. Cover reload restoration, tied values, invalid data, missing
columns, and storage-disabled browsers.

Exercise Rails' built-in Minitest integration

Add a stripped-down Rails fixture that runs bin/rails test with two
process-parallel Minitest workers. Synchronize one model test onto each
worker, then assert that SimpleCov records both subprocesses and merges
their coverage into a complete Rails-profile report.

Keep the conductor's merged report from hinging on runner luck

The rspec-conductor server stops forwarding a worker's output as soon as
that worker sends its run summary, so nothing SimpleCov prints from
at_exit reaches the command and these examples read the report files
instead.

Raise the reporting worker's sibling wait above its 60 second default,
since a saturated runner leaves the second worker writing its resultset
long after the server has both summaries in hand, and expiry there is
not a slow report but no report at all: SimpleCov skips result
processing outright once the wait gives up. That wait runs inside the
command rather than after it, because the server waits on worker exit,
so the command budget clears it with room for the merge on top.

A worker that is starved or killed outright never writes a resultset at
all, and no wait can conjure one. The outcome is settled by the time the
command returns, so check for the report right away and give the run one
clean attempt more, naming what the resultset held if a second worker
goes missing too.

Report a sandbox command timeout instead of its teardown

Killing a timed-out command unwinds out of the popen block, which closes
the stream the output reader thread is still blocked on and raises
IOError inside it. Ruby reports that on the thread's behalf, the suite's
warning capture treats it as an app warning, and the build fails with a
stack trace from the teardown rather than the timeout message that says
which command hung and what it printed. Stop the reader before unwinding
and keep its expected teardown quiet.

Let the tab strip own the report's top bar

Outline every group tab, so an unselected group reads as a tab rather
than as loose text floating above the panel. The selected one still sets
itself apart by filling with the panel's own colour and dropping its
bottom border, which merges it into the panel across the 1px the tab bar
overlaps.

Leave the colorblind and theme toggles unfilled. They keep an outline,
but taking the page background rather than the panel white puts them in
the same family as the unselected tabs, so the filled shapes in the bar
stay meaningful: the selected tab, and a toggle that is switched on.

Fade both ends of the tab strip. With more groups than fit, the strip
scrolls, and it used to guillotine whichever tab straddled an edge,
leaving a hard vertical cut against the controls. Trailing padding the
width of the fade keeps the last tab clear of it when everything already
fits, so nothing is dimmed that isn't overflowing. The leading edge has
no such padding to hide behind, since that would push the first tab off
the panel's flush left corner, so tab_scroll.ts marks the strip once it
has actually scrolled and the fade follows the class.

Drop the coverage glyphs from the source view and its legend

The gutter carried a plus, minus, tilde, plus-minus, or florin on every
line, and the legend swatches repeated them. They stated each line's
status without relying on colour, but they read as noise down the left
edge of every file and made the legend look like a key to a symbol set
rather than a sample of the colours themselves.

The gutter column existed only to hold the glyph, so it goes with them.
The line number keeps its per-status background, the line keeps its own,
and the swatches become plain chips of the colours the source view
paints, which is what a legend for a colour scheme should be.

Colour is now the only carrier of line status, so the Colorblind toggle
does the accessibility work alone: it swaps covered and missed for blue
versus orange, which is the pairing red/green vision cannot separate.

Refresh the report screenshots

Retake all of them against the current tab bar and source view, and add
the two pairings the formatter doc was missing: light mode, which the
README already showed but that page went straight past into dark, and
colorblind and dark together.

Colorblind mode no longer keeps non-color coverage markers, since the
gutter glyphs are gone, so say what the mode actually does instead.
Drop the trailing colons from the README's two captions as well.

Bump version to 1.1.1

Also bring the test_projects lockfiles back in step. Half of them still
pinned the path gem at 1.0.3, since the 1.1.0 bump only touched the root
lockfile, so a fixture run rewrote them and left the working tree dirty.

Serve each connection on its own thread with a read timeout

The serve loop handled connections serially and read requests with
unbounded blocking readline calls, so one stalled connection blocked
every other request. Browsers routinely open speculative sockets that
send no bytes, which made multi-second stalls easy to hit even
without a misbehaving client.

Each accepted connection now gets its own thread, and connection
reads carry a five second idle timeout so abandoned sockets release
their threads instead of pinning them forever.

The HTTP mechanics (request parsing, traversal-safe path resolution,
response writing) move to Serve::StaticFileHandler, leaving Serve
itself as the CLI wiring: option parsing, binding, and the accept
loop.

Align diff threshold and fail-on-drop with their documentation

The usage text promises that --threshold N lists files whose absolute
delta is at least N%, but the filter used a strict comparison, so a
file that moved exactly N% was silently dropped. The threshold is now
inclusive while the epsilon noise floor stays strict.

--fail-on-drop also failed CI when a file was deleted: a removed
file's deltas are all -baseline%, so removing a fully covered file
(dead code cleanup) tripped the gate even though no remaining file
regressed. Removed rows are still listed but no longer count as
drops, and the usage text says so.

Consolidate the CLI subcommands' shared plumbing

The mapping from a coverage criterion to its coverage.json fields
(lines_covered_percent, covered_lines, total_lines, and the branch
and method equivalents) was maintained three times in three shapes:
Coverage::CRITERIA, Uncovered::CRITERION_KEYS, and
Diff::CRITERION_FIELDS. A schema change needed three coordinated
edits. CoverageFile, the shared input boundary all three subcommands
already load through, now carries the single CRITERIA table and the
three local copies are gone.

The subcommands also re-declared the same --input/--json/--no-color
option trio four times, defined an identical one-line error helper
three times differing only in the command name, and printed the
human-readable stats row from the same format string in two places.
All three now live in CommandHelpers, which subcommand modules
extend. The error prefix derives from the module's own name, so a new
subcommand gets correct messages for free, and the uncovered parser
sheds its Metrics/AbcSize disable along the way.

Deduplicate configuration setters and artifact paths

minimum_coverage, maximum_coverage, and maximum_coverage_drop each
carried their own copy of the normalize-Numeric/validate/assign
sequence, and minimum_coverage_by_group inlined the same steps once
more per group. The four now share normalized_threshold, so the
setters stay behaviorally identical by construction and a future
change to the normalization lands in one place.

use_merging and enable_for_subprocesses duplicated the bodies of
merging and merge_subprocesses instead of delegating the way the
other deprecated aliases do, so a behavior change in the replacement
could silently diverge from its alias. Delegating also fixes
use_merging's return value: with merging disabled its final
expression was the skipped guard assignment, so it returned nil where
merging returns false.

existing_report_newer_than_us? built the .last_run.json path by hand
next to the LastRun helper that owns it, so a change to the file's
location would have to land twice to keep the deferred-report check
working. It now asks LastRun.last_run_path.

Make FileList empty-list behavior consistent

least_covered_file crashed with NoMethodError on an empty list
because the min_by result was cast and dereferenced unconditionally.
Result delegates the method publicly, so any caller holding a fully
filtered result hit the crash. It now returns nil.

never_lines and skipped_lines carried dead empty-list guards: sum
over an empty collection already returns 0, and the guards returned a
Float where the sum returns an Integer, so the return type depended
on whether the list was empty.

Fix comments that no longer match the code

The nocov chunk comment claimed the ranges were zero indexed, but
build_nocov_chunks numbers lines from 1 and the consumer subtracts 1.
The ResultsetFile doc said an empty file warns, but only the
unparseable case does, and it now also drops malformed entries. The
static extractor's visitor comment claimed its tuple ids match
Coverage's conventional shape, but the numbering order differs for
case/when and chained safe navigation. That is harmless since the
combiners intern on source span and reports drop ids, so the comment
now says exactly that.

Prune dead weight from the test suite

Eight of the thirteen step definitions in web_steps.rb are referenced
by no feature file: am on, go to, press, the regex variants of should
see, both should-not-see forms, show me the page, and print the page.
They came along with the generic capybara steps template. Removing
them also removes the file's only Lint/Debugger disable, and a
cucumber dry run confirms every step in the suite still resolves.
spec/fixtures/iso-8859.rb goes too: no spec, feature, or build script
mentions it, and the encoding examples in source_file_spec.rb
exercise the euc-jp and utf-8 fixtures only.

In the CLI specs, the --no-color assertion was copy-pasted across the
coverage, report, uncovered, and diff subcommands. It is now one
shared example that each colorization context feeds its argv, and it
additionally asserts the command produced output at all. The merge
examples each rebuilt the same a/b/merged/fixture paths inline, which
move to lets, and two minimum_coverage_by_group examples re-stubbed
warn on the config even though the describe's before block installs
exactly that stub.

Replace invalid UTF-8 bytes at source load time

A source file with no encoding magic comment is read as UTF-8-tagged
lines, and a stray high-bit byte (a Latin-1 comment in an otherwise
ASCII file, say) left the line invalid. The first regex to touch it,
the loader's own shebang check or any of the lines classifier's
patterns, raised ArgumentError: invalid byte sequence in UTF-8 and
took the whole report down.

The loader now scrubs invalid bytes to the Unicode replacement
character before any regex sees a line: the first-line reads are
scrubbed ahead of the shebang and magic-comment checks, and
ensure_remove_undefs scrubs UTF-8-tagged lines the same way it
already transcoded lines in other encodings. Every line therefore
leaves the loader as valid UTF-8, which classification, the JSON
payload, and the HTML viewer embedding all rely on.

With that guarantee in place, the JSON formatter's per-line
re-encoding became redundant work. It ran every line of every file
through an encoding converter, allocating a converted copy per line
on top of the chomp copy, the single biggest allocation source in
payload building for a large report. The formatter now embeds the
chomped line directly, and the invalid-bytes spec pins that
replacement characters still reach the JSON payload through the
loader's scrub.

Found by a large-project benchmark run whose formatter spec fed a
file with raw Latin-1 bytes through the pipeline.

Write the resultset cache as compact JSON

.resultset.json is a machine-read cache that every parallel worker
rewrites wholesale, and pretty printing nearly doubled the bytes
written, read back, and parsed on each of those store-merge round
trips. On a synthetic 100,000-file project the file shrinks from 89MB
to 51MB and serialization halves. Any JSON parser reads the compact
form, and jq covers the rare need to inspect it by eye.

Add a report pipeline scaling benchmark

Generates a synthetic project of N small files, runs SimpleCov over
it end to end in a child process, and prints per-phase wall-clock and
GC timings as JSON. Comparing two sizes an order of magnitude apart
should show phase ratios tracking the size ratio: at 10,000 versus
100,000 files every phase lands between 9.7x and 10.3x once GC time
is subtracted, so per-file cost is flat and the drift above 10x in
raw wall clock is garbage collection over the larger heap.

This is the harness that found the invalid-UTF-8 loader crash, the
per-line encoding converter copies in the JSON payload build, and the
pretty-printed resultset cache addressed in the preceding commits.

Make the serve handler and specs work on JRuby and TruffleRuby

Neither engine implements IO#timeout=, so the serve handler's first
line raised NoMethodError into the wide client rescue and every
connection closed with an empty response. Guard the call with
respond_to? and accept that an idle connection pins its thread on
those engines, which only leaks a thread in an interactive dev
server.

The cross-process lock spec gave the child one second to boot, but
JRuby and TruffleRuby take several seconds to start a subprocess.
Raise the boot timeout to 30 seconds and the warm reads to 10. The
spec also spawns its child with RbConfig.ruby instead of bare "ruby",
which resolves through PATH and can point at a different interpreter
than the one running the suite (for example a version manager shim
while the suite runs under JRuby). A mismatched child boots against
the suite's bundler environment and dies before printing its ready
line, while RbConfig.ruby always names the running interpreter,
matching what coverage_differential.rb already does.

The require_relative configuration spec eval'd its block with a
synthetic source file that does not exist. CRuby resolves
require_relative from the path string alone, but JRuby resolves it
through realpath and raised ENOENT. Use lib/simplecov.rb, a real file
that still lives outside spec/, so the assertion keeps its bite.

Fix the Windows spec failures and clean guard gap

The clean subcommand's safety guard only protected the cwd and the
project root by prefix comparison. On Windows the filesystem-root
spec stubs the coverage directory as "/", which canonicalizes to a
drive root the prefix comparison can miss, and the spec then really
executed rm_rf from the root of the runner's disk. That deleted the
checkout mid-run, which is why most other Windows failures showed
RSpec unable to read its own spec files. The guard now refuses any
path that is its own dirname (a filesystem root on every platform),
and the spec passes --dry-run as defense in depth so a future guard
regression fails loudly instead of destructively. With roots refused
up front, the trailing-separator ternary in descendant_of? became
dead code and is gone.

The remaining failures were genuine Windows semantics. AtomicFile
retries a rename that fails with EACCES on Windows, where a
destination open in a reader or mid-replacement by a concurrent
writer is not replaceable, matching what the concurrent-writers spec
exercises. The permissions spec now asserts against the mode chmod
actually recorded, since Windows widens 0400 to 0444. Two
configuration specs expand their expected paths because expand_path
prefixes a drive letter there. The failing-esbuild spec skips on
Windows, where its fake minifier (a POSIX shell script) cannot run.

Cut reflows in the HTML viewer's bar-width fit

equalizeBarWidths sized the coverage-bar column with a 1px-precision
binary search over a 80px range, ~7 iterations each forcing a full
table reflow. A reflow of a large file list is expensive, and on a
100,000-file report this was the single biggest cost of finishing the
load, close to a second on its own.

The table's width is not a clean function of the bar width (three bar
columns share the width variable and column min-widths make it step
irregularly), so the fit still has to be found by probing rather than
solved. Stopping the search once the bracket is within 8px instead of
1px roughly halves the reflows. 8px is imperceptible on a 160-240px
bar, and the search still returns a width that fits, so the table
never overflows any more than it already would when long file names
force it to the minimum. Verified across a viewport sweep that the
coarse result never exceeds the exact search's width (so never
overflows) and lands within 8px of it.

At a fixed 1440px viewport the finalize phase of a 100k-file report
drops from ~1000ms to ~855ms.

Keep the CSS mangler off BEM class modifiers

The HTML report's Covered column (line, branch, method) rendered
left-aligned with a wide gap before the Lines/Branches/Methods column,
so "5/" and "6" read as "5/    6" instead of the intended fraction
"5/6". The stylesheet had the right rules all along
(td.cell--numerator right-aligned, td.cell--denominator left-aligned),
but they never reached the page.

The asset build shortens CSS custom-property names to save bytes, and
its token regex /--[a-zA-Z][\w-]*/ also matched the --modifier suffix
of BEM class names. It rewrote the .cell--numerator / .cell--denominator
selectors (and .cell--coverage, .cell--number) to short aliases in the
CSS, but the mangler only touches CSS — the JS keeps emitting
class="cell--numerator" — so the renamed rules matched nothing and the
alignment (and a few other class rules) silently vanished.

Anchor the token to genuine custom properties with a negative lookbehind:
a custom property's -- always follows a separator, while a BEM modifier's
follows an identifier character. Real properties still mangle; class
modifiers are left verbatim so their rules keep matching. A spec pins the
split so the mangler can't eat class names again.

Add a cucumber feature for no-defaults mode

Requiring 'simplecov/no_defaults' before 'simplecov' sets
SIMPLECOV_NO_DEFAULTS so defaults.rb never loads, leaving a clean
slate. Nothing verified that it actually behaves that way. Two
scenarios pin the two observable effects against the faked_project:

- No default formatter: with only SimpleCov.start and no formatter
  configured, the run writes .resultset.json but no index.html and
  prints no "Coverage report generated" line.
- No default filters: the report keeps the two test files the default
  test_frameworks filter would drop (six files rather than four). The
  formatter has to be required explicitly too, since defaults.rb is
  what normally loads it.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/217.

Serialize live results with string criterion keys

A live result's coverage keeps Ruby's Symbol criterion keys while
entries parsed back from .resultset.json carry Strings, and the
combiners read only String keys. When two concurrent runners shared a
command name, the later writer's counts were silently dropped for every
file both sides carried, defeating the clobber-prevention merge from
https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/581. Stringify the
criterion keys in Result#to_hash so the stored and live shapes match.

Parse nested inspect segments in stored method keys

A singleton method defined on a plain instance (def obj.greet) records
its class as the nested inspect form #<Class:#<Object:0x...>>. The
quoting regex stopped at the first closing angle bracket, leaving a
dangling one that failed both Ripper passes, so merging or collating
stored resultsets with method coverage raised ArgumentError and crashed
the run. Recurse the pattern so nested segments are quoted whole.

Keep line-only directives out of method coverage

Method#skipped? fell back to asking whether all of the method's lines
were skipped, so wrapping a def in a simplecov:disable line block (the
README's own line-directive example) silently removed the method from
method totals. Route the deprecated :nocov: chunks through
SkipChunks#for(:method) like every other criterion, so MethodBuilder
marks those methods explicitly, and reduce the fallback to the
no-line-info case.

Require a word boundary after directive categories

The directive pattern matched a category name as a prefix of a longer
word, so a free-form reason like linear algebra reasons parsed as the
category line with the rest as reason. That narrowed the directive to
line coverage, the opposite of the documented behavior where
unrecognised text falls into the reason bucket and the bare form
over-disables everything.

Normalize group names in per-group threshold stores

group :Models normalizes the name to the String Models, but
minimum_per_group 95, only: :Models stored the Symbol untouched, and
the deprecated minimum_coverage_by_group setter kept Symbol keys too.
The check-time lookup then missed and the threshold was silently
unenforced, with only a confusing warning that the group does not exist
among available groups listing that very name. Run both stores through
GroupNames.normalize.

Gate diff --fail-on-drop on the same epsilon as display

Row inclusion and delta display both suppress deltas below EPSILON as
float noise, but coverage_drop? used a bare negative? check. A file
listed for a gain in one criterion could exit 1 over a 1e-14 drift in
another criterion, failing CI with only gains visible in the output.
Treat a drop as real only when it exceeds EPSILON.

Fold multi-statement paren conditions like the compiler

CRuby folds a multi-statement paren condition by its last expression
(Coverage emits no branch for if (1; 2)), but the extractor stopped
unwrapping at multi-statement bodies and synthesized a then/else pair
no run can ever hit. That is the permanently-missed phantom-tuple
failure mode the condition folding module exists to prevent.

The fold only happens when the compiler can eliminate every leading
statement of the sequence. Pinned against real Coverage on 3.2, 3.3,
3.4, 3.5, and 4.0: parse.y (3.2) eliminates only pure literals, the
3.3 compiler also eliminates side-effect-free reads and containers of
them, and the Prism compiler (3.4+) narrows containers to fully static
literals. Paren opacity applies to the last statement of a sequence
exactly as it does to a single wrapped literal. The new shapes are in
the runtime tuple equivalence battery and the fuzzer pool, so CI pins
them per version.

Skip the global config when HOME is set but empty

Some container and CI images export HOME as an empty string. That
passed the set-at-all guard, and File.expand_path then raised
ArgumentError (non-absolute home) out of require simplecov, so the gem
could not be loaded at all in those environments. Treat an empty HOME
like an unset one, keeping the ENV-based check because Dir.home raises
on JRuby when HOME is missing.

Harden the CLI subcommands' input validation

Three crashes become one-line errors. merge on a directory or
unreadable file raised EISDIR or EACCES with a backtrace because only
missing files and bad JSON were rescued, and the exist?-then-read pair
was racy besides. report crashed its emitters on valid JSON whose
total or groups had the wrong type. coverage crashed print_human when
the matched per-file entry was not an object.

Also consolidates the parse scaffolding the four read-only subcommands
each rebuilt (defaults hash plus OptionParser around common_options)
into CommandHelpers.parse_common.

Count dotfiles in clean's dry-run and reuse CommandHelpers

The dry-run entry count used a bare Dir glob, which skips dotfiles, so
a coverage directory holding .resultset.json and .last_run.json
undercounted what rm_rf would actually delete. Glob with FNM_DOTMATCH
and skip the directory's own dot entry. Clean also now extends
CommandHelpers instead of hand-writing its simplecov clean prefixes.

Polish the serve handler's edge responses

A malformed request line (missing the path token) raised inside the
wide rescue and closed the connection with an empty response, leaving
the defined 400 status text unreachable. Answer 400 explicitly. The
announced URL now brackets IPv6 hosts so --host ::1 prints a valid
address, and the deliberate non-percent-decoding of request paths is
documented as part of the traversal defense.

Guard against unusable PARALLEL_TEST_GROUPS values

Both built-in adapters computed the expected worker count with
ENV[...]&.to_i || 1, which returns 0 for a set-but-empty or
non-numeric value because 0 is truthy. A 0-worker expectation makes
the reporting worker's sibling wait return immediately, so it could
format before its siblings stored their results. Parse with
Integer(..., exception: false) and fall back to 1 for anything
non-positive.

The parsing and the parallel_tests-off opt-out guard both lived
identically in the two adapters; they now sit once in Base.

Close small robustness gaps in simulation and enforcement

SimulateCoverage rescued only ENOENT in read_lines and coverage_stub,
so a track_files glob sweeping up a directory named like a Ruby file
or an unreadable file crashed the merge step with EISDIR or EACCES.
Both now degrade to an empty file like a missing one.

CoverageViolations.compute_drop subtracted whatever type a hand-edited
.last_run.json carried, raising mid-at_exit for a string percent, and
lookup_group's misconfiguration notice went through Kernel#warn, which
-W0 swallows and Warning hooks intercept. The drop check now treats a
non-numeric value as missing, and the notice routes through
ExitCodes.print_error gated on print_errors like every other
enforcement message.

ResultsetFile.read swallowed files truncated to a single byte under a
length check, hiding exactly the corruption the module warns about. A
blank file still quietly means no results, but any other content flows
through decode, and the exist?-then-read race is gone.

Extract a shared base class for the exit-code checks

The five threshold checks each repeated the same skeleton: stash the
result and threshold configuration, fail when any violation exists,
memoize the violations, and loop them through a reporter. The new
ExitCodes::Check carries that shape once, so each check now declares
only its exit code, its CoverageViolations query, and its message
format. Also declares the RBS that the earlier CLI consolidation
commits should have carried.

Share the interned count-merge loop between combiners

BranchesCombiner.merge_branches and MethodsCombiner.merge_methods were
the same loop: intern each tuple, sum counts into [raw_key, count]
pairs, keep the first-seen raw key for display. It now lives once in
Combine::InternedCounts. The structural differences that are real
behavior (the nested condition-to-arms tables, the nil-preserving
method table) stay where they were.

Route cover filters through Filter.build_filter

build_cover_filter re-implemented the whole filter dispatch when its
only real difference from add_filter is glob semantics for bare
Strings. Filter.build_filter now takes a string_filter parameter that
also threads through Array elements, so the deliberate glob-vs-
substring divergence lives in one line and cover keeps its specific
error message by rescuing the generic one.

Clarify the eval threshold error and two stale comments

coverage :eval, minimum: 100 raised Unsupported coverage criterion
eval even though coverage :eval by itself is supported. The refusal
now says thresholds are the problem, and primary_coverage :eval gets
the same clear message. The defaults.rb comment claimed .simplecov
start calls are intercepted when they only draw a deprecation warning,
and the frozen /o interpolation of the nocov token is now documented
at its regexp.

Make the clobber-prevention backstop see failed child reports

The backstop that keeps an empty parent process from formatting over a
child's report keyed its freshness check on .last_run.json, which only
fully successful runs write. A rake parent therefore clobbered the
child's report exactly when the child's tests or coverage checks had
failed, which is when that report matters most. Result#format! now
touches coverage/.report_stamp no matter how the run ends, and the
backstop accepts either file as evidence. The exist-then-mtime race is
gone too, replaced by a rescue.

That rescue exposed a subtle at_exit hazard this commit also guards:
completing any rescue inside an at_exit handler resets $ERROR_INFO to
nil, so at_exit_behavior now captures the suite's exit status before
the deferral probe runs and hands it to run_exit_tasks!. Without that,
a failing suite read as clean after the probe and its failure exit
status was swallowed (caught by the return-codes fixture specs).

Restructure the documentation around a trimmed README

The README had grown to 1,617 lines. It now holds what a newcomer
needs (intro, getting started, example output, a configuration taste,
and a documentation index) in under 180 lines, written in a plain
voice without rhetorical flourishes. Everything else moved into topic
guides in a new docs/ directory: Configuration, Parallelism,
Formatters, CLI, and Troubleshooting.

The meta documents join them, clearing the project root down to
README.md and LICENSE: both changelogs, the contributing guide, the
code of conduct, the issue template, and the three link lists that
lived in doc/. Filenames follow one scheme, Title Case with lowercase
particles and underscores between words (Code_of_Conduct.md,
Alternate_Formatters.md, CLI.md). Underscores rather than hyphens
because GitHub matches community health files and issue templates by
those exact names apart from case, and it recognizes docs/ as a
location for them, so the code of conduct link, contributing prompt,
and new-issue template all keep working. LICENSE deliberately stays
at the root: GitHub license detection only scans root-level files,
and the gem packages it from there.

The alternate formatters catalog was rebuilt against the RubyGems
search results for simplecov (112 gems). Twenty formatters join the
twelve that were listed, organized by output type: terminal output,
HTML reports, machine-readable formats for CI and tooling, coverage
badges, and the build-your-own ERB route. The most notable addition
is simplecov-console, at twelve million downloads the most-used
formatter that was missing. Every entry was verified against
RubyGems and all new links checked live; simplecov-cobertura's moved
repository is also fixed.

Nothing under docs/ ships in the gem. The old doc/* glob is gone from
the gemspec, which drops the package from 197KB to 176KB, and the
changelog_uri metadata now points at docs/Changelog.md. Every
cross-document link was rewritten and verified to resolve with a
case-exact check, anchors included.

Add a colorblind-friendly mode and non-color coverage symbols

Red and green are the report's core signal, covered versus missed, and
they are the pairing most colorblind viewers cannot tell apart. This
adds two independent ways to read coverage without relying on that
distinction.

A Colorblind toggle sits to the left of the Dark toggle in the toolbar.
It swaps the covered and missed colors, and the coverage bands, for
blue versus orange, the standard colorblind-safe pairing, in both the
light and dark themes. Skipped stays yellow and the branch and method
misses keep their orange and purple, since those already read as
distinct hues. The choice persists in localStorage and is applied

Add end-to-end coverage for rspec-conductor parallel runs

rspec-conductor marks each forked worker with the parallel_tests
environment convention, TEST_ENV_NUMBER per worker plus
PARALLEL_TEST_GROUPS for the worker count (since rspec-conductor 1.0.7).
SimpleCov's generic parallel adapter already recognizes that convention,
so coverage from a conductor run merges into one report with unique
suite names per worker and no configuration.

Lock that support in with a dedicated test project and cucumber feature
covering the default numbering (first worker ""), the --first-is-1
numbering, branch coverage, and threshold checks deferred to the merged
report. Name rspec-conductor in the adapter docs so users can find it.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1156.

Share the parallel fixture between the parallel_tests and rspec-conductor features

The rspec_conductor test project was a byte-for-byte copy of the
parallel_tests one, differing only in which parallel runner its Gemfile
pulls in, and its feature repeated the expected coverage tables inline
three times. Any change to the fixture sources would have required
updating five copies of the tables and ten duplicated files.

Slim test_projects/rspec_conductor down to its Gemfile and Gemfile.lock.
A new setup step overlays those onto another project's sources, so the
conductor feature now runs against the parallel_tests fixture itself.
Rename the shared assertion steps to "the parallel fixture project"
(and their file to parallel_fixture_steps.rb) since they no longer
belong to a single feature, and reuse them in place of the inline
tables.

Keep exit tasks alive when a runner closes worker stdio before at_exit

rspec-conductor closes each worker's output pipes as soon as the worker
has sent its run summary to the server, before the worker's at_exit
hooks run. SimpleCov's exit tasks then died half way: the HTML and JSON
report files were already written, but emitting the status line probes
Color.enabled?, whose IO#tty? call raises IOError on a closed stream.
That exception aborted the rest of the at_exit work, so the minimum and
maximum coverage checks silently never ran under rspec-conductor, and
.last_run.json and the .report_stamp deferral marker were never written.

Treat a closed stream as not a tty in Color.enabled?, and drop the
status line in Formatter::Base#emit_status and the violation report in
ExitCodes.print_error when stderr is closed, instead of letting the
IOError cancel the threshold checks that follow.

The conductor feature's threshold scenario previously asserted that no
violation appears in the output, which the closed pipes made vacuous:
the text could never appear, and the swallowed worker exit status meant
the run always succeeded. It now asserts that .last_run.json carries
the merged 81.48. SimpleCov writes that file only when the threshold
check passes, and every single worker's partial slice is below the
threshold, so the file proves the check ran against the merged result.

Require coverage where Coverage.line_stub is called

SimulateCoverage and ResultAdapter both call Coverage.line_stub but
neither requires the coverage library, so they only work when another
code path has loaded it first. In a normal run start_tracking does
that, but a collate-only process never starts tracking. Today the
constant resolves by luck: the criterion-support check that
UnloadedFileInjector triggers happens to require coverage before the
line_stub call. Any reordering of that path turns into a NameError out
of SimpleCov.collate, so each file now requires what it uses.

Use anonymous block forwarding in the merge reference helper

The named block parameter added nothing: both methods only pass the
block straight through. Anonymous block forwarding works on every
supported Ruby (it arrived in Ruby 3.1), verified with a syntax check
and a smoke run on Ruby 3.2.11, and RuboCop's Naming/BlockForwarding
asks for this form once TargetRubyVersion reaches 3.4.

Add a bun test suite enforcing 100% coverage of the HTML frontend

The viewer's TypeScript modules are now tested with bun's built-in
runner against happy-dom, and bunfig.toml enforces 100% line and
function coverage on every run, the frontend counterpart of the
dogfood threshold the RSpec suite applies to lib/. The default rake
task and the typecheck workflow run the suite, and tsc now
type-checks the tests alongside the source.

Port every feature to spec/sandbox, driving the test_projects fixtures
in subprocesses through the SandboxProject harness. Browser assertions
become data assertions on the report payload embedded in index.html,
with rendering covered by the bun frontend suite.

Remove the browser-driving Aruba, Capybara, Cuprite, and Cucumber task
stack, the headless Chrome CI dependency, and the split CI test steps.
Keep Cucumber and Minitest as lightweight development dependencies
because copied fixture projects exercise their integrations from the
shared bundle cache.

Give each fixture subprocess a fresh Bundler activation with an explicit
copied or host Gemfile while retaining the host bundle path and excluded
groups. Cover both Gemfile paths so clean CI cannot leak the host
definition or lose its cached gems. The sandbox specs keep the old
platform envelope by skipping on non-MRI engines and Windows.

Fan the RSpec suite out across parallel workers

`rake spec` now runs the suite through parallel_rspec. The sandbox
specs spend nearly all their time waiting on fixture subprocesses, so
the suite parallelizes almost linearly (68 seconds serial, 17 in
parallel here), with a serial fallback where parallel_tests isn't
installed. Each worker scrubs the parallel_tests environment at boot
so command guessing, final-result detection, and spawned subprocesses
behave exactly as in a serial run, and per-worker tmp paths keep
coverage caches and warning captures apart. The dogfood coverage check
is now parallel-aware. Every worker stores its coverage slice as a
resultset-shaped partial, and the first worker waits for its siblings,
merges the slices through ResultMerger, and enforces the thresholds on
the union. Specs that asserted the literal tmp/coverage path now read
the configured directory.

Keep the conductor's merged report from hinging on runner luck

The rspec-conductor server stops forwarding a worker's output as soon as
that worker sends its run summary, so nothing SimpleCov prints from
at_exit reaches the command and these examples read the report files
instead.

Raise the reporting worker's sibling wait above its 60 second default,
since a saturated runner leaves the second worker writing its resultset
long after the server has both summaries in hand, and expiry there is
not a slow report but no report at all: SimpleCov skips result
processing outright once the wait gives up. That wait runs inside the
command rather than after it, because the server waits on worker exit,
so the command budget clears it with room for the merge on top.

A worker that is starved or killed outright never writes a resultset at
all, and no wait can conjure one. The outcome is settled by the time the
command returns, so check for the report right away and give the run one
clean attempt more, naming what the resultset held if a second worker
goes missing too.

Report a sandbox command timeout instead of its teardown

Killing a timed-out command unwinds out of the popen block, which closes
the stream the output reader thread is still blocked on and raises
IOError inside it. Ruby reports that on the thread's behalf, the suite's
warning capture treats it as an app warning, and the build fails with a
stack trace from the teardown rather than the timeout message that says
which command hung and what it printed. Stop the reader before unwinding
and keep its expected teardown quiet.

Outline every group tab, so an unselected group reads as a tab rather
than as loose text floating above the panel. The selected one still sets

but taking the page background rather than the panel white puts them in
the same family as the unselected tabs, so the filled shapes in the bar
stay meaningful: the selected tab, and a toggle that is switched on.

Fade both ends of the tab strip. With more groups than fit, the strip
scrolls, and it used to guillotine whichever tab straddled an edge,
leaving a hard vertical cut against the controls. Trailing padding the
width of the fade keeps the last tab clear of it when everything already
fits, so nothing is dimmed that isn't overflowing. The leading edge has
no such padding to hide behind, since that would push the first tab off
the panel's flush left corner, so tab_scroll.ts marks the strip once it
has actually scrolled and the fade follows the class.

Record which test covered each line

Coverage is a union over the whole suite. Every question past "is this
line covered" needs the other half of the data, which is which test
covered it. `track_tests` in a `SimpleCov.start` block records that map
and stores it in `.resultset.json` beside the merged coverage.

Recording samples `Coverage.peek_result` around each test and
attributes the delta, the lines whose execution count grew, to that
test. Only files under the project root are attributed, judged by the
same root regex the report's universe uses, since a peek covers every
gem the process loaded and diffing all of them on every test is what
would make tracking unaffordable. Counts are required, so
`:oneshot_line` is rejected at startup: a line reports only its first
hit ever, and every later test's delta would miss it. Tests overlapping
across threads cannot be told apart at all, because Coverage's counters
are process-global, so such a process warns and stores no map rather
than a misattributed one, while same-thread nesting still attributes to
both tests, which is the truth.

The data layer speaks of contexts rather than tests: a context is any
labeled region of execution, the mechanism coverage.py calls dynamic
contexts and the vocabulary a native Coverage feature would use, and
under `track_tests` every context is one test. The naive storage is
O(contexts times lines) strings, so ids are interned into a ContextMap
and each context's covered lines within a file pack into one Integer
bitmap, serialized as hex under a versioned `contexts` key so a future
format reads as absent instead of being misread. The map is exposed as
`SimpleCov::Result#contexts`, whose `covering(path, line)` answers
with the sorted ids. That query API is the seam the test-selection work
builds on, see
https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1264. The recorder's
contract (attribute or abstain, never guess) is deliberately separate
from its peek-diff engine, which is the part a native
`Coverage.supported?(:contexts)` engine would replace.

A merge has to either union the maps or drop them consistently rather
than silently keep one worker's, so every merge path applies the same
rule: the merged result carries the union when every merged result
recorded a map, and no map at all otherwise, with a warning when the
merge mixed tracked and untracked results. That covers the cross-suite
merge, concurrent same-command entries, and the forked collate, whose
workers now ship their slice's union back with their payload.

RSpec examples are wrapped by an around hook installed at start. The
Minitest wrapper prepends into `Minitest::Test`, through the bundled
plugin under minitest 5 and, under minitest 6, whose autorun no longer
discovers plugins, through a one-shot `Module#const_added` watch that
installs it the moment `Minitest::Test` is defined, so the canonical
helper ordering (SimpleCov first, minitest after) needs nothing extra.
Each test is identified by the location of its definition relative to
the root. Any other runner wraps its own units of work with
`SimpleCov.track_test`.

The thread poisoning, the format version, and the root-regex reuse are
adopted from the parallel work in
https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/pull/1275, as is building
each file's delta bitmap as one binary string rather than one bignum OR
per executed line.

Extracting Result's FilterConfig and serialization half into their own
files, and the parallel merge's worker payload into WorkerPayload,
makes room for the new code within the size limits and gives the pipe
format one owner.

Resolves https://github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1263.

Carry the context map into coverage.json under schema 1.1

The recording landed with no durable artifact: enable `track_tests`
and the map lived only in `.resultset.json`, an internal cache subject
to merge_timeout and `simplecov clean`, readable only from Ruby.
coverage.json is the schema'd public artifact downstream tools build
on, and this fork's CLI reads it rather than the resultset, so it is
the backend the who-covers and HTML work will consume.

The document gains a top-level `contexts` array of recorded ids, and
each file entry gains a `contexts` object of decimal index keys to
lowercase hex bitmaps, produced by the map's own wire encoding through
the new `ContextMap#serialized_bitmaps_for`, so the resultset and
coverage.json share one format owner. Presence follows the map's rule:
the array appears exactly when the formatted result carried a complete
map, an empty array means contexts were recorded and no test ran, and
an untouched file simply has no key, which under a present array
already says no recorded context executed it.

Adding keys to a contract whose schema declares
additionalProperties false is by definition a version bump, so this
mints schemas/coverage-v1.1.schema.json as the new versioned canonical,
bumps meta.schema_version to 1.1 for all output, points the unversioned
alias at it, and leaves coverage-v1.0.schema.json frozen for pinned
integrations. The new keys are optional, so documents from runs without
recordings stay exactly as small as before.

Answer which tests cover a file or line from the CLI

`simplecov tests` is the first consumer of the context data
coverage.json carries under `track_tests`. Bare, it lists every
recorded test. With a path it narrows to the tests touching that file,
and with path:line to the tests covering one line, decoding the
document's contexts array and the file's hex bitmaps. Only an all-digit
tail after the last colon reads as a line number, so Windows drive
colons and exotic filenames stay plain paths.

Text output is one test id per line and nothing else on stdout,
sorted, so the list can feed a runner directly
(simplecov tests lib/foo.rb:42 | xargs bundle exec rspec). An empty
answer keeps stdout empty and notes itself on stderr instead, and
--json emits a JSON array for tooling. A document with no contexts key
exits nonzero and says what to enable, since the likeliest reader is
someone who has not turned `track_tests` on yet. Malformed context
data poisons the whole answer rather than partially answering, the
same all-or-nothing tolerance the resultset reader applies.

Reading coverage.json rather than the resultset follows the CLI's
architecture: the resultset is a merge cache subject to merge_timeout
and `simplecov clean`, while coverage.json is the durable schema'd
artifact every other read-only subcommand consumes. Path arguments
match the way `simplecov coverage` matches them, by moving its lookup
into CoverageFile, the shared input boundary.

Cut tracking cost with segment recording

Recording now settles at segment boundaries. While consecutive
outermost tests map to the same context the tracker keeps one segment
open, and when the context changes a single snapshot closes one
segment and opens the next, so the suite pays one peek per context
change in run order instead of two per test. The price is that
in-root code running between two tests is attributed to the later
one. Between examples that window holds framework internals, which
the root filter already drops, so the map is unchanged in practice.
A nested track still opens with a fresh peek, the poisoned path still
peeks nothing, and the final segment is flushed against the run's
closing Coverage.result, since coverage is already stopped by the
time results are processed. The delta arithmetic moves into
TestTracker::Delta, which also memoizes the project-root check per
file, so the root regex runs once per file the process ever loads
rather than once per file per test.

On top of that, `track_tests granularity: :file` records one context
per test file (ids like spec/user_spec.rb, no line number), so every
test in a file shares one segment and the suite pays one peek per
change of file in run order, and test selection needs no more than
file identity anyway. How much that saves depends on the runner's
ordering: RSpec keeps a spec file's groups together, while Minitest
shuffles test classes globally, so a suite of many small classes
still changes file often.

Align the legend's swatches into columns

Each legend row was right-justified independently, so the single-item
rows landed wherever their label widths put them: the missed-branch
and missed-method swatches scattered along a ragged edge that made
the legend read as unrelated lines.

The legend is now one right-aligned box whose items sit in
left-aligned columns: the line row fills columns one through three,
and every single-item row takes the last column, so the trailing
swatches share one edge under "Missed line". Grid auto-placement
packs the rows, so any combination of enabled criteria lays out with
no gaps, and the layout-contract tests now describe the columns
design.

Keep each legend row level with its summary when it wraps

The legend box sized its own rows: compact rows packed at the top of
its grid area, level with the summaries only for as long as every
summary stayed on one line. In a narrow dialog a summary wraps onto
two lines, its header row grows, and every legend row below drifts
upward out of line with the row it describes.

The legend's rows are now the header grid's own row tracks, via
grid-template-rows: subgrid, so a wrapped summary grows the shared
track and its legend row stays beside it, aligned to the first line's
baseline. Each item is pinned to its row explicitly (subgrid
numbering is local, header row N is legend row N - 1), so a disabled
criterion's missing legend row cannot shift the ones below it. In
print the header falls back to document flow, where the subgrid
keyword behaves as none and the legend packs its rows as before.

Render the track_tests recording in the HTML source view

The report's source view speaks in status tints, so the recording's
headline signal becomes a new one: a covered line no recorded test
executed drains from green to a cool slate, with a Covered outside
tests chip in the legend. That is the coverage the issue called the
kind no assertion is looking at, produced by load time, suite setup,
or helpers, and the drain makes it glanceable without adding any
per-line furniture to a report that deliberately carries none. The
tint is near-achromatic on purpose, so it reads identically in the
standard, colorblind, and dark palettes.

Every executed line gains one quiet addition to the badge stack it
already has: a tests badge naming the covering count in words. It is
a real button, so the panel it opens is keyboard-reachable and takes
the report's focus ring for free. Clicking it expands an inline peek
panel beneath the line listing the covering tests, deliberately the
same ids in the same order that simplecov tests file:line prints, so
the report and the CLI give one answer; a click selects a whole id,
ready to hand to a runner. A drained line's panel explains the
absence instead of listing nothing. One panel is open at a time,
Escape closes it without closing the source dialog, and the panel
opts out of the line counter so numbering stays truthful. The file
header gains a Test coverage row with the file's distinct test count
and its drained-line count.

The viewer decodes the per-file hex bitmaps already embedded in the
report's coverage.json data (schema 1.1), nibble by nibble, lazily
per opened file. The data validator now checks the contexts shapes
when present and, like the viewer, demands nothing when absent: a
report generated without track_tests renders exactly as before.

files at 100%, descending ranks 90% covered by tests above 80%, and
ascending the reverse, before the filename settles exact ties. Cells
without the attribute (untracked runs, count columns) tie neutrally,
and the composite key still reverses cleanly, so the same-column
direction flip stays a pure reversal.

The count behind both is TestTracker's per-file bitmap union: covered
relevant lines no recorded context executed, computed once per file
on the raw hex bitmaps rather than a decoded per-line index, since
the file list pays it for every file on load. The source header's
"covered outside tests" figure now states the same attribution fact:
a no-test line whose colour a branch or method miss outranks was
excluded before, so the two views could disagree about the same file.

Split the line summary and covered chip by test attribution

The header's tests row spoke its own dialect ("Test coverage: 54
tests cover this file, 9 lines covered outside tests") next to three
rows that all say percent, fraction, remainder, and it restated line
counts the Line coverage row was already reporting. The two rows are
now one. A tracked report's line summary attributes its fraction:
"Line coverage: 100.00% 21/30 relevant lines covered by tests, 9/30
relevant lines covered outside tests, 1 missed", with the percent
still the file's line coverage in its band colour, the outside clause
in the drain's slate, and the missed clause unchanged.

The legend's covered chip splits the same way: green renamed
"Covered by tests", since that is what green means in a tracked
report, beside the slate "Covered outside tests", both in the line
row where covered always lived. The row anchors its columns counting
from its last item, so three chips untracked or four tracked, the
rightmost sits in the shared right column above Missed branch and
Missed method, and the header grid keeps the row numbering untracked
reports always had.

The per-file distinct-test count leaves the header with the old
phrasing, and the decoder's unused distinct field goes with it. The
per-line badges and the peek panel still name each line's tests.

and typecheck's rake assets:check rightly failed, most recently on
